correctness.rationale: For free Brownian excursions killed at L, the direct per-cycle success is exp(-z) and the interrupt-position resolvent is explicit. The conditional return success is exp(-z) times a positive hyperbolic-sine integral. Regenerative attempt decomposition proves the phase odds exactly. Positivity proves one and only one half-capture transition. The odds divided by z is an entire odd transform; its derivatives at zero produce all Hausdorff moments of h(L(1-sqrt(u))) and hence uniquely determine every continuous profile. For a regular return diffusion the boundary equation with positive splitting derivative uniquely recovers the drift as minus diffusivity times the logarithmic derivative of that splitting derivative. A polynomial nullspace preserves endpoints and strict positive first and second derivatives, yielding distinct smooth inward forces with finitely many identical odds. Finite diagnostics passed: 57 (including 54,000 bridge simulations). Numerical checks do not justify infinite assertions; every needed infinite step has an explicit proof.

originality.rationale: The earliest relevant work develops general stochastic-home-return renewal and explicit splitting and Green-function inputs (arxiv:2307.16294), so those forward identities are credited. The 2024 and 2026 papers study forward mean passage and speedup, not recovery of unknown return splitting from terminal phase labels. Materially inspected published inverse-source findings recover reset-location laws from MFPT target scans under instantaneous resetting, with different unknowns and observables. The core new result is that the full terminal-phase fraction as a function of Poisson rate is a compact odd-moment transform that injectively recovers every admissible return splitting profile and, at known diffusivity, its drift; in contrast any finite readings admit two distinct smooth inward forces. No found stronger theorem entails this complete inverse/finite-data classification. Publication-priority risk remains.
residual_risks: Standard linear inverse transforms and compact-moment uniqueness could appear in earlier unpublished/unindexed treatments of phase-resolved resetting, with distinct terminology.

The 2026 motivating article appendices were cross-referenced in the accessible rendering; not all separate source appendices were materially accessible, so an unexamined explicit inverse classification cannot be excluded.

value.rationale: Terminal phase tags are a concrete experimental observable even when stochastic return trajectories are inaccessible. The theorem identifies the full return splitting profile (and at known diffusivity the return force) solely from controlled reset-rate sweeps, proves a universal unique capture-majority rate, and establishes impossibility of finite-rate identification even in a physically natural smooth strictly inward-force class. This is a motivated inverse-response classification, not a gratuitous moment computation or a claim of statistical stability.
